title: Banaue Rice Terraces (Ifugao Rice Terraces)
summary: The Ifugao rice terraces in the Philippine Cordillera, northern Luzon, are stone- or mud-walled pond fields with irrigation drawn from mountain forests, built by the Ifugao. UNESCO inscribed five clusters in 1995, citing an age of 2000 years. The Ifugao Archaeological Project instead finds the rice-terrace systems likely emerged around A.D. 1600, so their age is disputed.

uncertainty.note: Contested: UNESCO says built 2000 years ago; the Ifugao Archaeological Project says A.D. 1600. The range allows both.

as_recorded.value: these intricate rice field systems likely emerged around A.D. 1600

when.display: Disputed: c. A.D. 1600 (excavation) or about 2000 years ago (UNESCO)

where.modern_name: Banaue, Ifugao Province, Cordillera, Luzon, Philippines (inscribed clusters lie in Banaue, Kiangan, Hungduan and Mayoyao)
where.historical_name: Ifugao highlands, Philippine Cordillera, northern Luzon

importance.justification: UNESCO-inscribed living cultural landscape and a case where excavation has challenged a long-cited age.

sources.title: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

reviewer_note: Coordinates are the Banaue municipality centre, not a terrace; the property is five clusters in four municipalities, so uncertainty is 30 km. Age is contested; the 2018 article says IAP excavations were concentrated in Kiangan.
